audit.whatIsWrong: The page's central instruction is wrong for this champion. breakdown.cooldowns and report[5] both say of Counter Strike: 'Dodges every auto and stuns - hold your damage until it ends', and winCon calls it 'the clock this lane runs on'. Counter Strike dodges incoming ATTACKS. Kassadin's damage is Null Sphere, Force Pulse and Riftwalk - abilities, not attacks - and all three land at full value while Counter Strike is active. Telling a Kassadin to hold his damage through it wastes the one window where Jax is standing still and committed.
audit.why: Riot's Counter Strike text: 'dodge all incoming attacks for a short duration and then quickly counterattack, stunning all surrounding enemies.' Attacks, not abilities. The correct instruction is narrower and much more useful: hold your AUTOS - including the Nether Blade reset, which is a basic attack - and keep casting. And the stun radius is only 300 units while Riftwalk covers 500, so the blink genuinely clears it rather than merely repositioning inside it.
audit.corrected: 'Hold your damage' replaced with 'hold your autos, keep casting' across the cooldown block, report[5] and mid; the 300-vs-500 range comparison added so the blink-out is concrete.
sources: champ-data/_kits/jax.json (E Counter Strike: 'dodge all incoming attacks', range 300, cooldown 17/15/13/11/9)
champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (R range 500; Q, E are abilities)

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is called 'Grandmaster's Might' in four places (spikes[3], wants.foe[2], late, whys[6]). Its name is Grandmaster-at-Arms. And no cooldown appears anywhere in either layer despite Counter Strike being named the clock the lane runs on.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9s - the longest cooldown in his kit and a seventeen-second window at rank 1, which is what makes 'punish the downtime' a real plan rather than a slogan. Leap Strike is 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s and Empower is 7/6/5/4/3s, so his gap-close and his damage buff both come back far faster than his stun - the stun is the only thing worth counting. Grandmaster-at-Arms is 110/100/90s. Riftwalk answers at 5/3.5/2s.
audit.corrected: The fabricated name removed from all four places and replaced with 'his ultimate' plus the 110s cooldown. The CORRECT name could not be written - see notes; the applier's elo-tier filter rejects any string containing the word that starts his real ability name. Counter Strike's 17s, Leap Strike's 8s and Empower's 7s also added.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Jax six of seven stages and Skill the seventh, so no stage reads Kassadin - while whys[5] says "you've reached even and start to tilt it" at First item and late says 'from 2+ items on, you are the one hunting him'.
audit.why: Kassadin wins this 56% over 25 games. Jax genuinely owns levels 1-5, but a chart with no Kassadin stage cannot produce that record, and two stages already have prose saying the lane has turned.
audit.corrected: First item set to Skill to match whys[5]'s 'reached even', and 2+ items flipped to Kassadin to match late and whys[6]. Levels 1-5 and Level 6 left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: early says 'Void Stone does almost nothing here, since Jax's combo is mostly physical' and stops there.
audit.why: Half true, and the missing half is the useful half. Grandmaster-at-Arms makes every third consecutive attack deal additional MAGIC damage, which is the part of an extended Jax duel that scales worst for you and the part your passive and Q shield actually bite on. Knowing which third of his damage is magic tells you when the shield is worth spending. Empower is also an auto-attack reset on a 7-second cooldown, so the wind-up on his weapon is the burst tell, not the ability cast.
audit.corrected: The magic third-strike on his ultimate named, and Empower's reset flagged as the tell.
sources: champ-data/_kits/jax.json (R: 'Every third consecutive attack deals additional Magic Damage'; W Empower: autoReset, cooldown 7/6/5/4/3)

Your only tool is Null Sphere, a short-range mana-hungry poke, and you have no escape, so do not step into his Leap Strike range to throw it. Last-hit at the tip of Q range, soak the harass, and accept you are conceding the lane — your job is to not die, not to trade. Void Stone does almost nothing here, since Jax's combo is mostly physical, not magic.

Bait that E with a Null Sphere or a feint, then punish the cooldown window once it whiffs.

A Kassadin following the old advice stands still through the one window where Jax is committed and stationary. Rewritten to 'hold the autos, keep casting'. WRONG ABILITY NAME, four places: Jax's ultimate was called 'Grandmaster's Might'. Per the kit file it is Grandmaster-at-Arms. Cooldowns added throughout - Counter Strike 17/15/13/11/9s (the only one worth counting, since Leap Strike is 8s and Empower 7s and both outpace it), Grandmaster-at-Arms 110/100/90s, Riftwalk 5/3.5/2s - and one concrete range comparison the page needed: Counter Strike's stun radius is 300 while Riftwalk travels 500, so the blink clears it rather than repositioning inside it. Empower is a 7s auto-attack reset, so the weapon wind-up is the burst tell. Fixed: breakdown.late called Null Sphere a silence. TOOLING BUG, needs your decision: Jax's ultimate is named Grandmaster-at-Arms in the kit file, but apply-proposals.js rejects any replacement text containing that name because its elo-tier filter (ELO regex in tools/apply-proposals.js line 43) matches the word 'grandmaster' as an elo tier. So the wrong name could be removed but the right one cannot be written by this pipeline - I substituted 'his ultimate' everywhere instead. Every Jax matchup across every champion has the same problem.
